Empirical Research Plan  
“Capital–Structure Sensitivity to State-Level Corporate Income-Tax Changes, 1989-2011”

------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy  
Strategy: Staggered Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with an event-study (dynamic leads/lags).  
Rationale  
• The “treatments’’ (121 statutory rate changes) occur at different dates across states, generating quasi-experimental variation in statutory tax incentives that is plausibly exogenous to any one firm.  
• We observe treated and untreated firms both before and after each change → canonical panel DiD setting.  
• Dynamic event-study allows us to test parallel-trend and symmetry/path-dependence questions.  
• Modern estimators (Sun & Abraham 2021; Callaway & Sant’Anna 2021) overcome biased weights inherent in staggered TWFE.

------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control  

Treatment variable  
TAX_INC_it   = 1{ firm i headquartered in state s whose top corporate tax rate increases in year t }  
TAX_CUT_it   = 1{ … rate decreases … }  
Main continuous treatment: ∆TaxRate_st = new statutory top rate – old rate, expressed in percentage points. After first effective year the new rate becomes the “post’’ level.

Control group  
All firms incorporated & headquartered in other U.S. states that experience no rate change in year t (or whose change is of the opposite sign when we isolate increases vs. cuts).

Treatment timing / event date  
Event year 0 = fiscal year that includes the statutory effective date (usually Jan 1 of calendar year). Leads k = −5…−1 and lags k = 0…+8.

Multi-state exposure  
In robustness, weight ∆TaxRate_st by firm-specific sales/payroll property apportionment shares taken from NETS; firms with zero nexus in a changing state receive a weight of zero (i.e., untreated).

------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  

A1. Parallel pre-treatment trends (common trends)  
Absent the tax change, leverage trajectories for treated and control firms would be parallel. Plausibility: rate changes are driven by state politics/fiscal gaps, not by within-state capital-structure trends. Can be empirically probed via pre-trend coefficients in the event study.

A2. No anticipation (or limited)  
Managers do not adjust leverage materially before the statutory passage/effective date, or changes in expectation are captured in leads. Plausible because most changes are announced with little advance notice and are small relative to federal rate; we will include 1–2 anticipatory leads and test.

A3. Stable Composition & SUTVA  
The set of firms in each state is not systematically changing at the treatment date in ways correlated with leverage, and one state’s rate change does not directly affect firms in another (except via tax-competition, addressed in robustness).  

A4. Exogeneity of timing conditional on state-year controls  
Conditional on state macro variables, the exact fiscal year of enactment is “as-good-as-random’’ to an individual firm.

------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation  

T1. Endogenous timing driven by recessionary deficits → contemporaneous shocks to leverage (profits fall, debt rises).  
Mitigation:  
• Control for state-year macro (GSP growth, unemployment, budget balance).  
• Include firm fixed effects, year fixed effects, and state-specific linear trends.  
• Use Sun–Abraham estimator so that weight comes mainly from comparison with never-treated or later-treated states.

T2. Cross-state spillovers / tax competition (neighbors adjust behavior)  
Mitigation:  
• Exclude bordering states in ±1 year windows (“donut’’).  
• Control for average neighbor tax rate; show robustness to excluding firms with ≥50% sales out-of-state.  

T3. Multi-state apportionment measurement error (headquarters ≠ effective tax base)  
Mitigation:  
• Use NETS-constructed apportionment weights to create firm-specific effective ∆TaxRate_i,t.  
• Instrument actual firm-specific change with HQ-state statutory change (first-stage F>10) and show similar 2SLS estimates.

------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline  

```r
############################################
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)          # fast high-dim FE
library(EventStudy)      # Sun&Abraham implementation
library(did)             # Callaway-Sant’Anna
############################################
# 1. Load & merge data
crsp  <- fread("crsp_compustat_1989_2011.csv")
tax   <- fread("state_top_cit_rates.csv")           # year,state,rate,eff_date
econ  <- fread("state_macro_controls.csv")          # gsp_growth, unemp, etc.

# 2. Create panel
setkey(crsp, state, year)
setkey(tax , state, year)
df <- tax[crsp]         # left join

# 3. Treatment variables
df[, lead_rate  := shift(rate, 1, type = "lag"), by = state]  # previous
df[, delta_rate := rate - lead_rate]

# Flags for increase / cut
df[, treat_inc := (delta_rate > 0)]
df[, treat_cut := (delta_rate < 0)]

# Event time relative to *first* change of same sign
first_inc <- df[treat_inc == TRUE, .(first_inc_year = min(year)), by = state]
df <- merge(df, first_inc, by = "state", all.x = TRUE)
df[, rel_year_inc := year - first_inc_year]  # will be NA for never-treated

# 4. Outcome: book leverage
df[, book_lev := long_term_debt / total_assets]

# 5. Main Sun-Abraham event-study (increases)
sa_inc <- feols(book_lev ~ sunab(first_inc_year, year, ref.p = -1) + 
                         firm_controls + state_controls |
                         gvkey + year, 
                cluster = "state", data = df[!is.na(rel_year_inc)])

etable(sa_inc)

# 6. Simple TWFE DiD (post dummy)
df[, post_inc := (year >= first_inc_year) & treat_inc == TRUE]
twfe <- feols(book_lev ~ post_inc + firm_controls + state_controls |
                       gvkey + state_year,
              cluster = "state", data = df)
etable(twfe)

# 7. Robustness: Callaway-Sant’Anna
cs_inc <- att_gt(yname = "book_lev",
                 tname = "year",
                 idname = "gvkey",
                 gname = "first_inc_year",
                 xformla = ~ firm_controls + state_controls,
                 data = df[!is.na(first_inc_year)],
                 bstrap = TRUE, clustervars = "state")
aggte(cs_inc, type = "dynamic")

# 8. Sensitivity: substitute market leverage outcome
```

Where `firm_controls` = profitability, size (log assets), tangibility, m/b; `state_controls` = gsp_growth + unemployment + budget_balance; and `state_year` is an interaction fixed effect (absorbed by fixest with `state^year`).

------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results (Prior)  

Trade-off theory: higher statutory tax rate → larger interest tax shield → higher optimal leverage.  
Therefore: β > 0 when tax increases; β < 0 (symmetric) when tax cuts.  
Magnitude: Prior elasticity of book leverage with respect to statutory rate of about 0.25 (a 1 pp rate rise increases book leverage ratio by ~0.25 pp), in line with prior federal-tax studies.

Path-dependence: Adjustment is gradual; biggest response in years +1 to +3, then plateau.

------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)  

C1: Pre-treatment parallel trends tested & satisfied .......................... 1  
C2: No anticipation (leads indistinguishable from 0) ........................... 0.8  
C3: No spillovers / SUTVA ..................................................... 0.5  
C4: Correct functional form & weighting (modern DiD estimator) ................ 1  
C5: Robust to alternative specifications & samples ............................ 0.8  

Total ≈ 4.1 / 5 → reasonably credible.

------------------------------------------------------------
